biggest_catch: HURR keeps a 15% lender commission on the full rental cost (rent + delivery + cleaning), and damage protection is only opt-in up to £50 of repairable damage - anything worse is the renter's problem to resolve, so lending high-value designer pieces still carries real loss risk, and earnings depend entirely on demand for your specific wardrobe.
catches: As a Lender you pay HURR a commission: default 15% of the total rental cost (Rental Fee + Delivery Fee + Cleaning Fee) on standard rentals; on FLEX rentals the commission is calculated on the Rental Fee alone. Renters pay a separate 15% default commission too.
Damage protection is opt-in and capped: it covers repairable damage up to £50 only; anything over £50 is the renter's responsibility. Lenders can set their own security deposits as extra protection.
Earnings are fully demand-driven: you set prices and availability, but income depends on brand desirability, size match, and local renter demand - most wardrobes earn little or nothing.
Items suffer wear, cleaning costs, late returns, and loss risk; you handle listing quality, packaging, and handover logistics.
UK platform (prices in GBP); rental income is taxable (UK £1,000 trading allowance may apply). Identity/account verification required.
No guaranteed bookings: lender testimonials on the site are marketing examples, not typical outcomes.

steps: Register as a HURR member and apply to become a lender (subject to HURR acceptance).
List wardrobe items you own (womenswear, accessories) with photos, rental price, and availability - no listing fee.
Set an optional security deposit on items for extra protection against damage or loss.
Accept incoming rental requests, arrange delivery or handover, and confirm item condition.
Get paid for each completed rental with the 15% lender commission deducted (opt-in damage protection covers repairable damage up to £50).
timing: Listing is free and self-serve; rentals booked on demand. Payout per completed rental with 15% commission deducted. First rental depends on item desirability and local demand.
